slides.title: PICO WebSpatial Academy
slides.body:
Take an ordinary website, make it spatial, and run it in the PICO OS 6 emulator. Claude Code does the typing.

Six levels, from an empty laptop to your own site floating in space. Every step has one action, the exact command or prompt, and what you should see.
slides.notes: Open on this slide while people settle. Press I for the level index, N to hide these notes, 0 to 5 to jump to a level. The follow-along link is this same page: it scrolls on a phone.

slides.title: Three facts before you start
slides.body:
Each one has cost someone an hour. Say them out loud.

- WebSpatial requires React. It works by replacing React's JSX runtime. There is no plain-HTML path today.
- WebSpatial needs PICO OS 6. The emulator is PICO OS 6 and has the runtime built in, so you open a URL and nothing gets packaged. A PICO 4 Ultra runs OS 5.x and shows a flat page.
- The SDK just moved to 2.0. `@webspatial/react-sdk` 2.0.0 is what the labs pin. We teach the 2.x API (`<SpatialBoot>`). Older guides use `@webspatial/vite-plugin` and `XR_ENV=avp`, which belong to 1.x.
slides.notes: Source: curriculum/SYLLABUS.md "Three facts before you start". If someone has a 1.x project, point them at curriculum/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#version-drift and move on.

slides.title: Six levels, three hours
slides.body:
Pass each lab's check before you start the next level. Press 0 to 5 to jump.

- L0 · Setup: 25 min in the room, 2 h self-paced, lab setup
- L1 · Hello Spatial: 25 min in the room, 1.5 h self-paced, lab labs/p1-hello-spatial
- L2 · Spatialize a website: 45 min in the room, 3 h self-paced, lab labs/p2-spatialize-site
- L3 · 3D + volumes: 30 min in the room, 2.5 h self-paced, lab labs/p3-volume-model
- L4 · Space Invaders in depth: 30 min in the room, 2.5 h self-paced, lab labs/p4-space-invaders
- L5 · Agentic expert: 25 min in the room, 4 h self-paced, lab labs/p5-capstone

L2 is the headline lab. The emulator install is pre-work: don't try to install Android Studio in the room.
slides.notes: Run of show from SYLLABUS.md: 0:00 L0 check-in (25), 0:25 L1 (25), 0:50 L2 (45), 1:35 break (10), 1:45 L3 (30), 2:15 L4 (30), 2:45 L5 (15 in the room), 3:00 end. L4 can be demo-only if the room is behind. Self-paced total is about 15.5 h.

slides.title: How the pieces talk
slides.body:
Four things on one machine. Claude Code drives all of them.

- Node + Vite serves your site on a port per lab (5301 for lab 1).
- PICO OS 6 emulator is a PICO device in a window, built on the Android emulator.
- pico-cli is PICO's one command line for the emulator, apps, logs, screenshots and perf.
- Claude Code runs pico-cli and the dev server, and asks the `pico-dev-knowledge` MCP about PICO docs.

The emulator opens your site at `http://localhost:<port>/`, mapped to your machine with `adb reverse`. `node setup/launch.mjs <n>` does the mapping for you.
slides.notes: The localhost-through-adb-reverse point comes back in every level; land it here once. MEASURED on the OS 6 emulator (emulator-lab + labs-builder, 2026-09-24): http://10.0.2.2:<port>/ loads but reports isSecureContext=false, beforeinstallprompt never fires, and the page stays a flat tab. localhost through adb reverse is a secure context, and Lab 1 installed as com.picoxr.webapp.localhost.* with depth. PICO's docs say 10.0.2.2; the measurement overrides them for this workshop (assets/pico-docs/WEB-APP-RUNTIME.md section 3, kit CLAUDE.md, setup/launch.mjs).

- Our path: a React website, spatialized with WebSpatial, opened as a Web App in the same emulator.

slides.title: Setup: Claude Code, Node, pico-cli and the PICO OS 6 emulator
slides.body:
25 minutes in the room, because the install is pre-work. 2 hours self-paced.

- Why the emulator, not a headset: WebSpatial needs PICO OS 6. The emulator is OS 6. A PICO 4 Ultra is OS 5.x.
- Emulator machine: Windows 10/11 or an Apple Silicon Mac, 16 GB RAM (32 GB is comfortable), about 40 GB free disk, an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 or better.
- Below that bar? You take the web-only track: every lab runs flat in a desktop browser.
- Git, and Node 20.19+ or 22.12+ (Vite 8's floor). A paid Claude plan for Claude Code.
- Licence: the PICO Emulator and PICO WebSpatial browser are PICO-licensed. PICO has cleared tonight's attendees to use both.
slides.notes: Sources: curriculum/L0.md, SYLLABUS.md prerequisites, setup/SETUP.md. The kit recommends Node 24 LTS. Claude Code needs a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise or Console account; the free plan doesn't include it. The full install walk-through is setup/SETUP.md; exact versions are in setup/DEPENDENCIES.md.

- Already on a newer release? Install 2025.1.4.8 beside it. Don't uninstall anything.

slides.title: 16 GB of RAM? Do this before you boot.
slides.body:
The emulator reserves 6 GB by default. On 16 GB, make room first.

- Close Chrome, Slack, Android Studio and anything else heavy.



- With the emulator stopped, set this in `~/.pico/avd/<avd name>.avd/config.ini`:
slides.notes: Close other web apps before launching a lab: at 4 GB the emulator's low-memory killer closes them. A 16 GB laptop booted this way on 2026-09-24; page rendering at 4096 is still being confirmed. Source: setup/SETUP.md step 13 and the kit CLAUDE.md. Windows path: %USERPROFILE%\.pico\avd\PICO_6.0.avd\config.ini. "Insufficient RAM free" goes to stderr only, never the emulator log. labs/EMULATOR-RESULTS.md measured about 2 GB of free commit on a 16 GB laptop with Chrome, WSL and node running, against 6,144 MB needed.

slides.title: Checkpoint: you are set up when...
slides.body:
Every box ticked, or a written reason next to it.

- `npm run doctor` names your track, and `pico-cli doctor` is clean or explained.
- `pico-cli emulator status` shows a running emulator, or you're on the web-only track.
- You know your device id (usually `emulator-5554`).

slides.title: Hello Spatial: your first WebSpatial app
slides.body:
A website becomes an app in the room. You keep writing HTML and CSS.

- Not WebXR. WebXR gives you a canvas and a head pose, and you draw every pixel. WebSpatial gives the OS your HTML to render next to other apps.
- Window scene: a 2D panel for GUI. It keeps the same apparent size, so text stays readable.
- Volume scene: a box with real depth, in metres, for showing an object.
- React is required. The SDK hooks React's JSX runtime. A static .html file never passes through it.
- No packaging on PICO OS 6. Run the dev server, open the URL, install it as a Web App from the address bar.

slides.title: A browser tab is flat. A Web App has depth.
slides.body:
WebSpatial only switches on inside PICO OS 6's Web App Runtime. The button in the address bar is the door.

## Browser tab
- Your page, in a PICO Browser tab.
- Flat. `enable-xr` and `--xr-*` do nothing here.
- `display-mode` is `browser`.

## Web App
- Install it from the address bar: the monitor icon, titled Install app on OS 6.0.0 (PICO's docs call it Open as standalone app).
- Depth. WebSpatial switches on: elements lift, `window.open` opens new windows.
- Needs a secure URL: `localhost` via `adb reverse`.
- `display-mode` is `standalone` or `minimal-ui`.
slides.notes: PICO's docs (assets/pico-docs/WEB-APP-RUNTIME.md, from developer.picoxr.com/document/web/webspatial/ and /install-free/): "In the Web App Runtime of PICO OS 6, any WebSpatial API used in your page source is automatically activated." The button only appears when the URL falls inside a Web App's manifest scope. No install needed for development, and no WebSpatial Builder on PICO. webspatial.dev calls the same button "Run as a standalone app"; PICO's label is "Open as standalone app".

slides.title: What the Web App needs
slides.body:
No install, no depth. Two things decide whether the page can become a Web App.

- A secure URL. In the emulator open `http://localhost:<port>/` through `adb reverse`; `node setup/launch.mjs <n>` sets this up. 10.0.2.2 loads but was not a secure context in our test (no install); use localhost.
- A manifest with the 4 required fields: `name` (or `short_name`), `icons`, `start_url`, `display`. Link it with `<link rel="manifest" href="/app.webmanifest">` and serve it as JSON (`application/manifest+json`).

To see the adb reverse it will run, without running it:
slides.notes: MEASURED on the OS 6 emulator (emulator-lab + labs-builder, 2026-09-24): http://10.0.2.2:<port>/ loads but reports isSecureContext=false, beforeinstallprompt never fires, and the page stays a flat tab. localhost through adb reverse is a secure context, and Lab 1 installed as com.picoxr.webapp.localhost.* with depth. PICO's docs say 10.0.2.2; the measurement overrides them for this workshop (assets/pico-docs/WEB-APP-RUNTIME.md section 3, kit CLAUDE.md, setup/launch.mjs). Manifest rules: developer.picoxr.com/document/web/manifest/ via WEB-APP-RUNTIME.md section 4. PICO requires display (it's optional on some other platforms). `scope` decides which URLs count as the app, and so where the button shows. On a real PICO OS 6 device HTTP needs Developer Mode plus a debug broadcast; not tonight's concern.

slides.title: Show which runtime you're in
slides.action: Put a badge on the page that says browser or webapp.
slides.expect:
In a browser tab the badge says browser, and nothing pops out: that's expected.
Installed as a Web App it says webapp, and enable-xr elements lift.

slides.title: The whole recipe, in four lines
slides.body:
No vite-plugin. No XR_ENV. One bundle; PICO is detected at runtime from the user agent.

After the four steps below, mark something: `<div enable-xr>` with `position: relative`, `--xr-back: 80` (px) and `--xr-background-material: translucent`.
slides.notes: Source: labs/VERSIONS.md and the p1/p2 lab READMEs. @webspatial/vite-plugin 1.0.1 aliases the SDK to /web, which 2.0 removed, so builds fail with it. Proven on the OS 6 emulator by emulator-lab (2026-09-24): lab 1's solution, installed as a web app, reported UA ... PicoWebApp/0.4.0 ... WebSpatial/1.5.0, react-sdk 2.0.0, and spatialized its enable-xr card (the screenshot on "Make it pop out").

slides.title: Scaffold the app
slides.action: Ask Claude Code to scaffold a Vite + React app wired for WebSpatial 2.x.
slides.body: Doing it by hand? These two are the start:
prompts: Scaffold a Vite + React + TypeScript app in ./hello-spatial wired for WebSpatial 2.x: install @webspatial/react-sdk and @webspatial/core-sdk, set jsxImportSource to @webspatial/react-sdk in tsconfig.app.json, wrap the root in <SpatialBoot>, add public/app.webmanifest (name, start_url /, display minimal-ui, a 512 any icon and a 1024 maskable icon) linked from index.html, set react({ jsxImportSource: '@webspatial/react-sdk' }) in vite.config.ts, and make sure npm run dev:xr binds 0.0.0.0. Run the dev server and tell me the URL the emulator should open.
slides.notes: The next three slides are what that one prompt does, so people can check Claude's diff against them. Don't install @webspatial/vite-plugin: that's the 1.x setup.

slides.title: Route JSX through the SDK
slides.action: Set jsxImportSource in two places: the tsconfig that holds "jsx", and vite.config.ts.
slides.expect:
Every <div> you write in JSX now goes through WebSpatial's createElement, which is what understands enable-xr and --xr-back.
If enable-xr does nothing later, suspect this step first.
slides.notes: In Vite's template the tsconfig is tsconfig.app.json (curriculum/L1.md); the labs use a single tsconfig.json. The vite.config line comes from the kit CLAUDE.md: Vite 8 transforms with oxc and ignores esbuild.jsxImportSource, so without it every enable-xr goes inert with no error. curriculum/L1.md only shows the tsconfig half.

slides.title: Boot it and add the manifest
slides.action: Wrap the app in <SpatialBoot> and link a PWA manifest.
slides.body: The manifest needs `display` set to `standalone` or `minimal-ui`, plus a 1024 maskable icon with no transparency. Without a valid manifest the browser can't install it as a Web App.
slides.expect: In a desktop browser the app looks normal. <SpatialBoot> only loads the spatial half inside a WebSpatial runtime.
slides.notes: <SpatialBoot> renders nothing while it loads and has no fallback prop, so put loading UI outside it. Add onError={e => console.error(e)} if the emulator shows a blank page.

slides.action: Start lab p1's dev server in the background and open it in the emulator, from the kit root.

slides.notes: launch.mjs runs `adb reverse tcp:<port> tcp:<port>` and opens http://localhost:<port>/ in the emulator. It only calls pico-cli web launch to install the PICO browser if it's missing, because web launch rewrites localhost to the flat 10.0.2.2 URL. It refuses any target that isn't an emulator. slides.title: Never point web launch at a real headset
slides.body:
pico-cli web launch is for the emulator only.

- It installs a 336 MB PICO WebSpatial browser APK on the target before it opens anything.
- It rewrites localhost to 10.0.2.2, which exists only inside the emulator and isn't a secure context there either.
- Both are right for the emulator and wrong for a headset. A PICO 4 Ultra runs OS 5.x and has no WebSpatial runtime anyway.
- On this emulator image it also fails (`INSTALL_FAILED_UID_CHANGED`): the browser is a system app it can't update.
- Use `node setup/launch.mjs <n>`: `adb reverse` plus localhost, and it refuses any target that isn't an emulator.
slides.notes: Source: kit CLAUDE.md "Emulator and pico-cli rules" (pico-cli 0.5.0, source-read) and TROUBLESHOOTING.md. The lending headsets on the table are someone else's fleet: installing an APK on one is a change to their device.

slides.action: In the address bar, just left of the star, click the monitor icon, titled Install app on OS 6.0.0 (PICO's docs call it Open as standalone app). Then Install.
slides.body:
- Install app dialog: click Install. The app opens in its own window with a glass background.
- Wait up to 60 s; if the panels are still missing, close and reopen the app once. Panels arrive late on a cold launch. Don't judge at 5 s.
- Next time, open it from its own tile on the home launcher, not from the browser.
slides.expect: The app opens as its own window. Within 60 s the enable-xr card floats in front of the page (if not, close and reopen the app once).

slides.title: 3D and volumes
slides.body:
WebSpatial puts 3D inside a 2D layout. A 3D container takes part in CSS layout as a flat plane, and its content lives in a box in front of it.

- `<Model>` shows a prebuilt GLB or USDZ file. Its API follows the web `<model>` element.
- `<Reality>` composes a scene from primitives, materials and model entities as React components.
- Volume scene: a window that behaves like a physical object, sized in metres.
- Units flip: `--xr-depth` is px, entity sizes and positions are metres, rotation is radians.

slides.title: Spatial Invaders: depth as gameplay
slides.body:
So far depth has been decoration. Here it carries meaning: a complete, flat Space Invaders game where Z tells part of the story.

- Rows stand in terraces, back rows deepest.
- The formation comes toward you as it descends.
- Your shots fly away from you; enemy shots fly at you.
- A hit row flinches forward before the invader vanishes.
- A HUD window and a hall of fame window, synced over `BroadcastChannel`.

slides.notes: The showpiece. Source: labs/p4-space-invaders/README.md (final). start/ is solution/ with every SPATIAL line removed, so `git diff --no-index labs/p4-space-invaders/start/src labs/p4-space-invaders/solution/src` is the whole lesson. Collisions never read Z: the game plays the same on a laptop. The screenshot is desktop Chrome (flat); the corner badge says "Browser tab · flat".

slides.title: Where everything sits in Z
slides.body: Each row writes its absolute depth: `(5 + y × 0.08) + row × 20 + flinch`. Nothing is nested. At wave 1 (y = 80) the front row is 11.4 + 80 = 91.4 px. Keep depths modest: planes lifted far toward you, low in the window, fall below it.

diagrams.title: Side view of Spatial Invaders: five row planes at stepped depths that come forward together, the shield line and the ship
diagrams.description: Side view with the window's glass on the left at depth 0 and the player on the right; --xr-back grows toward the player. No spatial element sits inside another: each of the five rows is its own top-level plane at an absolute depth of 5 plus 0.08 times the formation's Y, plus row times 20, so row 0 (the top row) is deepest and all five come forward together as the formation descends. A hit row flinches 24 px forward. The shield line is one plane at 100 and the ship is at 120, always the closest. Player shots travel from 120 back to the front row; enemy shots travel from the firing row toward the ship. The Fire and arrow buttons are flat on the window.

slides.notes: Start y is 80 (solution/src/constants.ts START_Y), per wave +14 up to wave 5. Numbers from labs/p4-space-invaders/README.md "The depth map (solution)" and solution/src/depth.ts: rows ROW_STEP 20, formation 5 + y × 0.08, shields 100, ship 120 (the deepest the front row ever reaches is 5 + 412 × 0.08 + 80 = 118), flinch 24 with POP_DECAY 0.85 (about 200 ms), overlay card 150 while shown, buttons flat. The first version used ship 260, shields 210 and 30 px steps, and in the emulator's default view the ship and buttons projected below the window's bottom edge. All values are px, one decimal, never negative, written through refs by writeBack(el, z), which skips unchanged values.

slides.title: The layer budget: 11 planes, not 230+
slides.body:
Each enable-xr element is its own native plane. Spatialize containers, not sprites.

| Layer | Planes | Depth (px) |
|---|---|---|
| Rows 0 to 4 | 5 | `(5 + y × 0.08) + row × 20` |
| Invaders (55) | 0 | ride on their row |
| Shields | 1 | 100: four bunkers on one plane |
| Ship | 1 | 120, always the closest |
| Shots, bombs | 4, pooled | travel in Z |
| ◀ Fire ▶ | 0 | flat on the window; pinch = click |
| Playfield | 0 | plain div: no nesting |

11 planes (12 with the overlay card) vs 230+ if every sprite were spatial.

slides.title: Agentic expert: Claude Code runs the loop
slides.body:
Every step you did by hand is a command, so an agent can run them. Your job is to hold it to evidence.

- The loop: edit, serve, `pico-cli web launch`, capture, `pico-cli log -l W`, judge against SPEC.md, repeat.
- Evidence per claim: a screenshot path, a log line or a DevTools read. "The code looks right" isn't evidence.
- Bound it: an iteration cap and a stopping condition.
- Ground it: PICO questions go through the `pico-dev-knowledge` MCP, with a cited source.

Its bundled docs predate SDK 2.0, so don't run it inside the labs; in your own project, run it and then add one line to CLAUDE.md: 'SDK 2.0: wrap the app in <SpatialBoot>; labs/VERSIONS.md overrides .webspatial/docs' It also adds a .git/info/exclude entry, and `npx @webspatial/starter` (the scaffolder) creates an SDK ^1.5.0 project (examples/README.md). In a 2.0 project that steers Claude away from <SpatialBoot>, which means back to flat pages. slides.title: Troubleshooting: "it looks flat"
slides.body:
| Symptom | Check / fix |
|---|---|
| Flat in a browser tab | A tab is never spatial. Install it: the monitor icon, titled Install app on OS 6.0.0 (PICO's docs call it Open as standalone app), just left of the star → Install |
| Installed, still flat | Wait up to 60 s; if the panels are still missing, close and reopen the app once |
| Second window blank | The page is wrapped in `enable-xr`; remove it |
| Some panels render, others don't | An `enable-xr` nested inside another `enable-xr`: it never renders on PICO OS 6.0.0. Un-nest |
| No install offered at `10.0.2.2` | 10.0.2.2 loads but was not a secure context in our test (no install); use localhost. `node setup/launch.mjs <n>` opens localhost for you |
| No install offered at localhost | Manifest missing, unlinked, or lacking `name` / `start_url` / `icons` / `display` |
| Changed the manifest, nothing changed | The installed app keeps the old one: uninstall (`adb uninstall <pkg>`) and install again |
| Volume or window opens flat at 1280×720 | `initScene` ran before boot finished, so it did nothing. Register scenes in `<SpatialBoot onReady>` |
| Installed, UA has `WebSpatial/`, still inert | App not wrapped in `<SpatialBoot>`: in 2.0 spatial code loads only inside it |
| Still inert with `<SpatialBoot>` | `jsxImportSource` missing in the tsconfig or in `react({ jsxImportSource })` in `vite.config.ts` |
| One element won't lift | No `enable-xr`, or no `position: relative / absolute / fixed` |
| Glass looks solid | Your own `background` covers the material; clear it in spatial mode |
slides.notes: Root cause and first five rows: labs/SPATIAL-CRACK.md (VERIFIED on the OS 6.0.0 emulator, 2026-09-24): only an installed Web App's UA contains WebSpatial/, and the SDK checks for exactly that. Other rows: curriculum/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

slides.title: Troubleshooting: setup and the emulator
slides.body:
| Symptom | Check / fix |
|---|---|
| PICO Spatial plugin won't install | Android Studio must be 2025.1.x, not the latest |
| Emulator dies: `QEMU main loop exits abnormally` | Not enough free RAM; the real message is on stderr. Use the 16 GB recipe |
| "Site can't be reached" at `localhost:<port>` | Dev server not running, or the `adb reverse` mapping is gone (it resets when the emulator restarts): rerun `node setup/launch.mjs <n>` |
| Still unreachable | Wrong port, or the firewall blocks Node on private networks |
| Knowledge MCP stopped answering | `pico-cli setup` ran while sessions were open; restart Claude Code |
| Install fails, logcat says `manifest is empty` | Manifest icons rejected (seen with one SVG icon): ship PNG icons with real `sizes` (192, 512, 1024 + maskable) |
| Web app closes on its own | At 4 GB the low-memory killer: close other web apps before launching a lab |
| One screenshot is mostly black | Capture artefact, not your page: use `node setup/snap.mjs` (burst) |
| HUD misses a message sent as it opened | Chrome drops a BroadcastChannel post made in the same task as `window.open`: post, then `setTimeout(() => window.open(url, name), 100)` |
slides.notes: Rows from curriculum/TROUBLESHOOTING.md "Setup and emulator" and "Reaching the dev server", plus the kit CLAUDE.md screenshot rule.
